title: Compare Semantic Versions
oneLiner: Write a comparison function for semantic versions such as 1.10.0, 2.0.0-rc.1 and 1.0.0+build.5, following the SemVer rules for numbers, pre-releases and build metadata, and use it to sort.
keyTakeaway: Never compare versions as text. Compare MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH as numbers; a pre-release (after -) sorts before the release itself; pre-release parts compare numerically when both are numbers, as text otherwise, with numbers first; and build metadata (after +) is ignored. A comparison function returning -1, 0 or 1 then plugs into any sort.
explanation:
Write CompareVersions(a, b), which returns -1 if version a comes before b, 0 if they have the same precedence, and 1 if a comes after b. Versions look like MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, optionally followed by -PRERELEASE and then +BUILD, for example 1.10.0, 2.0.0-rc.1 and 1.0.0-beta.11+exp.sha.5114f85. All inputs are valid.

The rules, from the Semantic Versioning specification: first compare MAJOR, then MINOR, then PATCH, as numbers (so 1.10.0 is after 1.9.3). If those are equal, a version with a pre-release comes before one without (1.0.0-rc.1 is before 1.0.0). If both have pre-releases, split them at the dots and compare part by part: two numeric parts compare as numbers (beta.2 before beta.11), two text parts compare by character codes (so "B" comes before "a"), and a numeric part comes before a text part. If every compared part is equal, the one with fewer parts comes first (alpha before alpha.1). Build metadata after + is ignored completely, so 2.1.0+build.5 and 2.1.0 compare as 0.

Each test reports [CompareVersions(first, second), the whole list sorted with your function]. The sort is stable, so versions that compare as 0 keep their original order. Use string.CompareOrdinal for text parts in C# (culture-aware comparison would sort "a" before "B"); Python's < on strings already compares code points. In Python the checker sorts with functools.cmp_to_key(compare_versions).

visualizationSteps.message: MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH are equal as numbers: go on to the pre-release.
"beta" and "beta" are text parts and equal.
11 and 2 are both numeric, so compare them as numbers: 11 > 2. As text, "11" would wrongly come first.
So CompareVersions returns 1: beta.11 comes after beta.2. And 1.0.0 itself comes after every 1.0.0 pre-release.

complexity.note: Comparing two versions splits and scans both strings once: linear in their length L, with the split parts taking O(L) space. Sorting n versions with it is O(n log n) comparisons.
